season.term: Taman Tunku Abdul Rahman + Tunku Abdul Rahman Park + Manukan
season.source: Google Trends, Malaysia (hand-exported CSV, terms summed)

visitors.title: Tunku Abdul Rahman Park visitors (all five islands)
visitors.note: 2026 is partial (to August) and left out. 2020 to 2022 are depressed by COVID closures and caps.

prov.basis: Average visitors per day (visitors divided by 365) against the effective carrying capacity of the park's three busiest islands (Manukan, Mamutik, Sapi), which take about 96% of visits.

caps.label: Central: 1,867 (ocean-based, the tighter of the two limits)

rows.label: Festive peak day: about 2,000 visitors (press report)

caveats: This is an academic estimate, not an official Sabah Parks limit (Sabah Parks said it would set one but no figure was found).
The abstract does not state the time unit; it is taken to be visitors per day, as is usual for this method. Check the full thesis before relying on it.
Visitor counts cover all five islands; the capacity figures cover three. The study also defines separate regular, high and festive season values that are not broken out in the abstract.
The tighter ocean-based limit is used as central because both land and sea limits must hold at once.
